This report summarizes the multi-period difference-in-differences pipeline. It is generated after running `python scripts/run_pipeline.py`, which creates the cleaned panels and the result tables used below.

## Group shares and treatment effects

The treatment cohorts are unevenly sized. The first treated cohort is the largest group, and the later cohorts have negative cohort-specific average treatment effects.

| group | fraction | att |
|---|---:|---:|
| cohort_5 | 0.4400 | 0.1773 |
| cohort_6 | 0.1160 | -0.4791 |
| cohort_7 | 0.0440 | -0.4115 |
| cohort_8 | 0.0400 | -0.2108 |
| all_treated | 0.3516 | 0.0263 |

## TWFE comparison

The key scalar comparisons from `output/results.json` are:

| quantity | value |
|---|---:|
| twfe_no_covariate_trend | -0.0310 |
| twfe_covariate_trend | -0.2743 |
| event_study_no_covariate_simple_att | -0.2340 |
| event_study_covariate_never_simple_att | -0.4683 |
| event_study_covariate_notyet_simple_att | -0.4568 |

## Brief interpretation

The cohort-event DID estimates compare each treated cohort with units that are valid controls for the specific target period. This keeps the estimand tied to a particular cohort and event time, so the signs and magnitudes reflect the treatment-effect heterogeneity built into the data-generating process.

The pooled TWFE coefficient residualizes the outcome and treatment using unit and time effects, then compresses all timing variation into one coefficient. With staggered adoption and heterogeneous effects, already-treated cohorts can implicitly help identify effects for later cohorts, and the resulting coefficient is not the same object as the average of the cohort-event treatment effects. This is why the TWFE values differ from the simple post-treatment event-study averages above.
